texts.preamble: Vivek Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr on 28 March, 2018 1 Mcrc-12100-2018 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Mcrc-12100-2018 (Vivek Jain Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh) Gwalior, Dated : 28.03.2018 Shri Brajesh Kumar Sharma, counsel for the applicant. Shri B.P.S. Chauhan, Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State. Case diary is available. This is first application under Section 438 of CrPC for grant of anticipatory bail.
texts.arguments: It is submitted by the counsel for the applicant that he has been made an accused on the basis of confessional statement made by the co-accused, which is not admissible in law. Per contra, it is submitted by the counsel for the State that on an information given by an informer, the co-accused was arrested from the spot, from whose possession a huge quantity of spurious ghee was found and he has stated that the said spurious ghee was supplied by the present applicant.
texts.petitioner_arguments: It is submitted by the counsel for the applicant that he has been made an accused on the basis of confessional statement made by the co-accused, which is not admissible in law. Per contra, it is submitted by the counsel for the State that on an information given by an informer, the co-accused was arrested from the spot, from whose possession a huge quantity of spurious ghee was found and he has stated that the said spurious ghee was supplied by the present applicant.
